_comment: The game families on the library page. make-notes.py builds one landing page per family, in a folder named by its id. A game in this repo is named by its folder (its README.md and teaching.json are read from there); a game with its own live site gives url, readme (a path to its README in a sibling repo, read at HEAD), and teaching inline.

families.name: Maze games
families.blurb: Two Pac-Man mazes, played from both sides. In Chomp & Spell you eat letters and spell words with them; in Haunt you are the ghosts.

families.name: Shooting games
families.blurb: Four shooters: a maze with the lights out, a five-beam horizon drawn two ways, and a city by the sea under attack.

families.name: Dodge-'em games
families.blurb: Get across, or get up, without getting hit: toads crossing a road on a rainy night, and a climber on a twelve-floor building.

families.name: Adventure games
families.blurb: Explore and find things: draw a dungeon and walk through it, or document the animals of the Amazon rainforest by lantern.

games.name: Dragonkeep
howto: You win by not killing the dragon
games.intro: Draw a dungeon floor plan and walk through it. Volume, surface area, and a dragon you win by not killing.

practice: Measuring a floor plan as they draw it: area, perimeter, volume, wall area and surface area update with every cell.
Same volume, different wall: two rooms with the same area can have very different perimeters.
Surface area is not additive: push two rooms together and the shared wall stops being surface.
The square-cube law: double every dimension and the volume grows eight times while the wall grows four.
teaching.thinking: A floor plan raised to a ceiling height is a prism. Students draw the prism, the game measures it, and then they walk through it, so every number is something they can see and step through.
